subject: Acme POC Kickoff & Next Steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC Kickoff & Next Steps

Hi John —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we're aligned before kickoff: 

Pain points you shared
- Customer service latency on complex troubleshooting tickets; average handle time is ~22 minutes for L2 escalations.
- Inconsistent redaction and PII handling across existing automation.
- Cost of in-house models spikes at peak hours; infra ops burden is high.

Goals for the pilot/POC
- Reduce L2 mean handle time by 30% on pilot ticket subset (billing + integrations).
- Maintain PII redaction compliance to your policy (retain zero PII in logs).
- Measure per-inference unit cost and target a 25% reduction vs current infra at 99th percentile load.

Scope (proposal)
- 6-week POC targeting billing & integrations queues (~2k tickets/month).
- Deliverables: prompt set + eval harness, mocked production traffic run, quality regression dashboard, cost/latency report.

Success metrics
- Accuracy: >= 85% correct classification/routing for L2 cases (on your eval set).
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency < 300ms for streaming responses.
- Cost: target <= 75% of current per-inference cost given similar throughput.

Owners & timeline
- Acme owner: John Doe (Product Ops), Jane Smith (Security) cc’d.
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (Sales lead), Rishi Malhotra (Solutions/POC), Aditya Rao (Infra onboarding).
- Week 0 (now): access & data checklist, scope sign-off.
- Week 1: prompt set & eval design, endpoint access.
- Weeks 2–4: integration + baseline runs.
- Weeks 5–6: quality tuning, final report + handoff.

Access/setup steps (what we need from Acme)
1) S3 access to anonymized ticket exports (or sample CSV) — minimum 2k rows.
2) A test service account or API key for internal routing tests.
3) Security questionnaire entry & contact for SOC/infra scan scheduling.

I attached a draft scope matrix and a quick checklist for onboarding. If this looks good I'll send a formal SOW and kickoff calendar invite.

Attachments: acme-poc-scope.xlsx, redwood-poc-setup-checklist.pdf

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

——

Subject: Re: Acme POC Kickoff & Next Steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Agreed on the goals and scope; the metrics look realistic. A couple of clarifications: 
- For PII redaction we need a short compliance appendix that outlines how telemetry and KV cache are handled and what data is stored/never stored. Jane, can you confirm the SOC/Security checkpoint cadence?
- Procurement: we need a short commercial summary (term sheet) and an estimate of monthly cost for the pilot window to get internal approval.

We’ll provide the anonymized ticket export by EOD Wednesday. Procurement is looped in — procurement@acme.com has the PO template we’ll use.

Also, please add Rishi as the technical contact for infra/setup.

John

- redwood-poc-setup-checklist.pdf (security appendix & access checklist)
- acme-poc-scope.xlsx (draft scope matrix with owners & acceptance criteria)

Quick answers: 
- Security appendix covers telemetry retention (7 days for debug logs by default, option for 0 retention), KV cache is not persisted to S3 and per-tenant keys are rotated per your KMS policy. We’ll redact PII at the ingestion layer — details in the PDF.
- Commercial summary: we’ll send a 1-page term sheet today (estimated pilot cost = $6,500 / month for the reserved baseline + overage rates). That should be enough for procurement to start internal approvals.

Next steps I’ll take this week: 
1) Send SOW + 1-page term sheet (by EOD Tue)
2) Kickoff calendar invite for Fri 3/20 — 60 minutes (Rishi to lead technical run-through)
3) Rishi to share onboarding link and test credentials format (by Wed)

If that timeline works I’ll lock the invites.
